'''Jannero Pargo''' (born October 22, 1979) is an American professional [[basketball]] coach and former player who serves as an assistant coach for the [[Indiana Pacers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played college basketball for [[Neosho County Community College|Neosho County CC]] and the [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas Razorbacks]].

==College career==
Graduating from [[Chicago]]'s [[Paul Robeson High School (Chicago, Illinois)|Paul Robeson High School]] in 1998, Pargo played collegiately for the [[University of Arkansas]] after transferring from [[Neosho County Community College]] in [[Chanute, Kansas]] in 2000.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Gross |first=Larry |title=Sports |work=Chicago Defender |date=December 3–5, 2004 }}</ref>
Jennero was known at Arkansas for casually dribbling across the half court line and burying a deep 3-pointer. He produced several 30 point games during his tenure and was ahead of his time by firing up 3-pointers from anywhere on the floor, and hitting them, which has become commonplace in the NBA.

==Professional career==

===Early years===
From 2002 to 2008, Pargo played in the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] for the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], [[Toronto Raptors]], [[Chicago Bulls]] and [[New Orleans Hornets]]. During the 2008 playoffs with the Hornets, he garnered attention by coming off the bench for star [[Chris Paul]].  He averaged 10.3 points in 12 playoff games and hit big three-point shots in game 7 of the Western Conference Semifinals against the Spurs.

===Europe===
After the [[2007–08 NBA season]], Pargo signed a one-year, $3.8 million contract with the [[Russian Professional Basketball League|Russian League]] team [[MBC Dynamo Moscow|Dynamo Moscow]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/pargo-play-russia-115900252--nba.html|title=Pargo to play in Russia|date=August 15, 2008 |access-date=January 19, 2018}}</ref> In January 2009, Pargo secured a buyout from his Russian club and signed with the [[HEBA A1|Greek League]] club [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/43122/180/reds-add-jannero-pargo-to-backcourt|title=Reds add Jannero Pargo to backcourt|access-date=January 19, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3861932|title=Pargo moving on from Moscow to Olympiacos|date=January 26, 2009|website=ESPN.com|access-date=January 19, 2018}}</ref> He was released by Olympiacos on May 5, 2009. He averaged 3.5 points and 1.4 assists per game in the [[Euroleague]].

===Return to the NBA===
On July 13, 2009, Pargo signed a one-year deal with the [[Chicago Bulls]], bringing him back to the Bulls and the NBA for a second time.

On September 24, 2010, he signed with the New Orleans Hornets. However, he was released before the start of the regular season because of his slow recovery from knee surgery.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nola.com/hornets/index.ssf/2010/10/new_orleans_hornets_release_ja.html|title=New Orleans Hornets release Jannero Pargo; knee injury rehab slow and was well behind Willie Green|access-date=January 19, 2018}}</ref>

On March 20, 2011, Pargo re-signed with the Bulls.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/lucas_pargo_signed_110320.html |title=Bulls sign John Lucas III and Jannero Pargo |work=NBA.com| date=March 20, 2011| access-date=March 16, 2013}}</ref>

On December 16, 2011, Pargo was waived by the Bulls.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-waive-guard-jannero-pargo.html |title=Bulls waive guard Jannero Pargo |work=NBA.com|date=December 16, 2011|access-date=March 16, 2013}}</ref> On December 20, 2011, Pargo signed with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/pargo_122011_pr.html |title=HAWKS SIGN JANNERO PARGO |work=NBA.com|date=December 20, 2011|access-date=March 16, 2013}}</ref>

On October 1, 2012, Pargo signed with the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-sign-jannero-pargo |title=Wizards Sign Jannero Pargo |work=NBA.com|date=October 1, 2012|access-date=March 16, 2013}}</ref> On November 15, 2012, Pargo was released by the Wizards to make room for Shaun Livingston.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-sign-shaun-livingston |title=Wizards Sign Shaun Livingston|work=NBA.com|date=December 15, 2012|access-date=March 16, 2013}}</ref>

On January 21, 2013, Pargo signed a 10-day contract with the Atlanta Hawks after injuries to [[Lou Williams]] and [[Devin Harris]] decimated their depth at the point guard position.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-sign-jannero-pargo-10-day-contract |title=ATLANTA HAWKS SIGN JANNERO PARGO TO 10-DAY CONTRACT|work=NBA.com|date=January 21, 2013|access-date=March 16, 2013}}</ref> On February 2, 2013, he signed a second 10-day contract with the Hawks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-sign-jannero-pargo-second-10-day-contract |title=ATLANTA HAWKS SIGN JANNERO PARGO TO SECOND 10-DAY CONTRACT|work=NBA.com|date=February 2, 2013|access-date=March 16, 2013}}</ref>

On March 14, 2013, Pargo signed a 10-day contract with the [[Charlotte Bobcats]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bobcats/news/bobcats-sign-guard-jannero-pargo-10-day-contract |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130411110549/http://www.nba.com/bobcats/news/bobcats-sign-guard-jannero-pargo-10-day-contract |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 11, 2013 |title=Bobcats Sign Guard Jannero Pargo to 10-Day Contract |work=NBA.com |date=March 14, 2013 |access-date=March 16, 2013 }}</ref> On March 24, 2013, he signed a second 10-day contract with the Bobcats,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bobcats/news/bobcats-sign-guard-jannero-pargo-second-10-day-contract|title=Bobcats Sign Guard Jannero Pargo to Second 10-Day Contract|work=NBA.com|date=March 24, 2013|access-date=March 24, 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130328105946/http://www.nba.com/bobcats/news/bobcats-sign-guard-jannero-pargo-second-10-day-contract|archive-date=March 28, 2013}}</ref> and on April 3, 2013, he signed for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bobcats/news/bobcats-sign-guard-jannero-pargo-remainder-season |title=Bobcats Sign Guard Jannero Pargo for Remainder of Season |work=NBA.com |date=April 3, 2013 |access-date=April 3, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130406074602/http://www.nba.com/bobcats/news/bobcats-sign-guard-jannero-pargo-remainder-season |archive-date=April 6, 2013 }}</ref> On August 9, 2013, he re-signed with the Bobcats.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bobcats/news/cats-re-sign-pargo |title=Cats Re-Sign Pargo |work=NBA.com |date=August 9, 2013 |access-date=August 9, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130815121404/http://www.nba.com/bobcats/news/cats-re-sign-pargo |archive-date=August 15, 2013 }}</ref> In April 2014, the Charlotte Bobcats were renamed the Hornets.

On July 25, 2014, Pargo re-signed with the Charlotte Hornets<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/hornets-re-sign-pargo|title=Hornets Re-Sign Pargo - Charlotte Hornets|website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=January 19, 2018}}</ref> to a reported fully guaranteed one-year, $1.45 million contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/234350/Jannero-Pargo-Re-Signs-With-Hornets-On-One-Year-Deal|title=Jannero Pargo Re-Signs With Hornets On One-Year Deal|access-date=January 19, 2018}}</ref> In his 2014–15 season debut on November 9, 2014, he became the first modern-day player to play for both the New Orleans Hornets and Charlotte Hornets franchises.

Pargo's final NBA game was played on December 22, 2014, in a 110 - 82 win over the [[Denver Nuggets]]. Pargo recorded 6 points and 1 assist in his final game. For the next 6 weeks, Pargo would not play any games and would eventually be waived by the Hornets on February 4, 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/hornets-sign-williams-waive-pargo|title=Hornets Sign Williams, Waive Pargo - Charlotte Hornets|website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=January 19, 2018}}</ref>

===NBA Development League===
On February 2, 2016, Pargo was acquired by the [[Oklahoma City Blue]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/transactions/ |title=NBA D-League Transactions |work=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. |access-date=February 2, 2016 |url-status=unfit |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160203051824/http://dleague.nba.com/transactions/ |archive-date=February 3, 2016 }}</ref> and after rehabbing a left ankle sprain, he joined the team on March 31.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/okc-blue-adds-jannero-pargo/n-5117460|title=OKC Blue Adds Jannero Pargo|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=March 31, 2016|access-date=March 31, 2016}}</ref> That night, he made his debut for the Blue in a 122–117 loss to the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]], recording 13 points, one rebound and two assists in 16 minutes off the bench.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20160331/RGVOKL/|title=Vipers Stop Blue On Road|work=NBA.com|date=March 31, 2016|access-date=March 31, 2016|archive-date=April 14, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160414114431/http://dleague.nba.com/games/20160331/RGVOKL/|url-status=dead}}</ref> On February 23, 2017, Pargo was waived by the Blue.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/dleague/teams/Oklahoma-City-Blue/38/Transaction_History|title=Oklahoma City Blue Transactions History|work=REALGM.com|access-date=February 25, 2017}}</ref>

=== The Basketball Tournament (TBT) (2017–present) ===
In the summer of 2017, Pargo played in [[The Basketball Tournament]] on [[ESPN]] for team A Few Good Men (Gonzaga Alumni). He competed for the $2 million prize, and for team A Few Good Men, he scored 21 points in his only game played. Pargo helped take team A Few Good Men to the Super 16 round, where they then lost to Team Challenge ALS 77–60.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thetournament.com/bracket|title=Bracket {{!}} The Basketball Tournament|website=www.thetournament.com|language=en|access-date=February 27, 2018|archive-date=May 14, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190514091135/https://www.thetournament.com/bracket|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Coaching career==
On September 15, 2017, Pargo was named as an assistant coach for the [[Windy City Bulls]] of the [[NBA G League]].,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.csnchicago.com/chicago-bulls/former-bulls-guard-jannero-pargo-joins-windy-city-bulls-coaching-staff|title=Former Bulls guard Jannero Pargo joins Windy City Bulls coaching staff|date=September 15, 2017|access-date=September 15, 2017}}</ref> On July 1, 2019, Pargo was named an assistant coach for the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/story/2019/7/1/blazers-finalize-2019-20-coaching-staff|title=Trail Blazers Finalize Coaching Staff for 2019-20 Season|date=July 1, 2019|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 1, 2019}}</ref> On August 9, 2021, Pargo was named an assistant coach for the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-announce-staff-additions|title=Pacers Announce Staff Additions|date=August 9, 2021|website=NBA.com|access-date=August 9, 2021}}</ref>
